KRW's archive gives one card at each hundredth of λ from zero to one, showing how disclosure and expected wrong directions move together.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **λ .25 & λ .01.** The published race card states 1,324 pairs (E/N .136); at the first positive λ (.01), no pair is stated.
- **λ .08: first race split.** Genuine Parts stands above the other 96 firms at risk .07406.
- **λ .30, λ .98 & λ 1.** At .30, 830 pairs become stated and 92 withheld; stated pairs dip from 4,620 (.97) to 4,614 (.98) and reach all pairs at λ 1 (DR = E/N = .268).

<details>
<summary>Archived path and figure notes</summary>

KRW's code selected the grid cards using their archived probabilities and solver tolerances; the app holds those grades fixed and evaluates them with the released postrank probabilities. Baseline race card: Figure 7; gender card: Figure 14 (§VIII); Figures 5A and 6 (§V.E); Figure 10A (§VI.B).

</details>
